system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student in computational genomics and protein biology who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given experiments that compare ESM-2 protein language model embeddings vs Evo2 DNA language model embeddings for encoding functional gene class information. Two gene sets were tested: (1) DNA repair vs tumor suppressor genes (178 genes), (2) glycolysis vs T-cell signaling genes (189 genes). Key results: On DNA repair vs TSG, ESM-2 achieves AUROC 0.894 vs Evo2's 0.78 with an MLP probe, but both show flat unsupervised geometry (silhouette~0, ARI~0). On glycolysis vs T-cell, ESM-2 achieves AUROC 1.0 (5-fold CV, permutation p=0.01) vs Evo2's 0.91 CV AUROC, with ESM-2 showing meaningful unsupervised separation (silhouette=0.186, distance ratio=0.776). The core finding: protein sequence embeddings (ESM-2) encode functional class information more strongly than DNA sequence embeddings (Evo2) across both gene sets, and the degree of separation depends on the functional contrast — metabolic/immune distinctions are more strongly encoded than DNA repair/TSG distinctions. In all cases, functional information is latent rather than geometrically obvious (unsupervised clustering fails even where supervised probing succeeds strongly). IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS: (1) Do NOT add new gene classes. (2) Reuse cached dataset.json and embeddings from run_0/data/. (3) Do NOT propose layer ablation. (4) Focus on: the protein vs DNA modality comparison, what drives the difference between the two gene set contrasts, and the supervised vs unsupervised geometry gap.
